plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Whole streets in eastern Australia turn lavender-blue as this tree's trumpet-shaped flowers open in huge clusters. When the blooms fall, they cover pavements and lawns in a purple carpet.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring, from early to mid October. The trees reach full bloom in November in Sydney.
plants.funFact: The jacaranda is native to South America. Its Australian spring bloom is so well known that people link it to the start of exam season and to the arrival of warmer weather.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This evergreen shrub opens silky pink, rose or white flowers when most gardens are winding down for winter. Its petals surround a bright boss of golden stamens, and the blooms last for weeks of cool weather.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn into early winter. Many varieties start in November and continue through January.
plants.location: Native to Japan. Widely grown in temperate gardens across Asia, Europe and North America.
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Its seeds are pressed in Japan to make camellia oil.

plants.name: Chrysanthemum morifolium
plants.description: Chrysanthemums fill autumn gardens and temple displays with dense, layered pompons and spidery, shaggy blooms. In Japan, this is the season of chrysanthemum shows, where growers display prized plants trained into perfect domes.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn. Flowering runs from about September through November, and it can start earlier in warmer zones.
plants.location: Japan and temperate gardens across East Asia, Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums bloom in response to long nights, not to temperature. Growers can shift the flowering date by controlling how much light the plants get. The flower is the emblem of the Japanese Imperial family.
